segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Hey, quick check on the Kenridge proposal. They asked for the 28-seat extension through April 30, 2027, right?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, 28 seats, same support tier, and procurement wants the quote at $54,600 before noon their time tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Okay. Are you waiting on pricing approval or legal language?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Neither, which is the annoying part. Producing this one extension means I have to take the same account name, seat count, start date, end date, discount, billing contact, and PO note and retype it into the pricing sheet, then the quote tool, then the contract workspace, then the billing intake, and then deal desk asks for the same fields again in their form. If one date is off, the quote and agreement don't match, so I’m checking them side by side. I started yesterday after the customer call and I’m still not through the last approval screen. It’s like five separate apps for a no-change renewal.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yeah, that tracks. For the discount, it’s the standard 12 percent off list, not anything special?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Correct. List is $62,040, net is $54,600 rounded, annual invoice, net 30. No services, no add-ons.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Good. If you send me the final PDF before you route it, I’ll sanity check the dates and dollars.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Appreciate it. The customer’s buyer, Renee, also asked that the invoice reference PO 41873 and ship-to stay as their Denver office.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Got it. And go-live doesn’t matter because they’re already live, just continuity from May 1?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Exactly. I’ll get you the draft by 4:30, assuming the last approval clears.
